title: Annotatio III §.XI open (7): Sense — bread and wine not annihilated; body and blood not corporally substituted
pass_a_gloss: §. XI. (7.) To cleaner Sense, and not to one only but to several: For that bread and wine in the Sacred Eucharist are not annihilated, nor in their place Christ’s body and blood corporally substituted, sight and touch as well as taste and smell distinctly prove; Whose distinct testimony, especially when offered by all together, is by no means to be called into doubt.
pass_b_english: §.XI (7): cleaner Sense — not one only but several.

Sight, touch, taste, and smell distinctly prove bread and wine are not annihilated in the Eucharist, nor Christ’s body and blood corporally put in their place; their joint distinct testimony is not to be doubted.
source_text: §. XI. (7.) Sensui emunitiori nec uni tantum, sed pluribus: Enimvero panem & vinum in S. Eucharistia non annihilari, nec in horum locum, corpus & sanguinem Christi, corporaliter substitui, tàm visus & tactus, quàm gustus & olfactus, distinctè evincunt; Quorum distinctum testimonium præsertim ab omnibus unà perhibitum, in dubium vocandum haud esse.
